newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-INJURY-HIT RANGERS CANNOT AFFORD CELTIC DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-INJURY-HIT RANGERS CANNOT AFFORD CELTIC DEFEAT.

text.p: If Rangers do make it nine successive Scottish league titles, they are likely to cross the championship-winning line at the end of the season at a stagger rather than with the assured ease of a winning thoroughbred.
For Walter Smith's beleaguered team go into Sunday's potential title-decider against Old Firm rivals Celtic with almost as many players in the treatment room as on the training ground.

The situation is so desperate that Smith has re-signed 35-year-old former Rangers striker Mark Hateley a year after selling him to Queen's Park Rangers to lead his front line in Sunday's match at Celtic Park.

Rangers are preparing for the make-or-break game with strikers Erik Bo Andersen (skull fracture), Gordon Durie (appendicitis), Sebastian Rozental (knee surgery) and Peter Van Vossen (knee injury) all out of action. Durie was taken ill after Rangers lost 2-0 to Dundee United on Wednesday and spent Thursday in hospital on a drip.
He was expected to be allowed out of hospital on Friday but would appear to have little chance of playing. The other strikers have no chance of regaining fitness in time.

Rangers will also be without goalkeeper Andy Goram, who has been playing with a rib injury for two weeks. He will be replaced by Manchester City reserve keeper Andy Dibble, signed on a temporary contract as cover last Wednesday. But Dibble has not played a first-team match for months and an Old Firm derby against Celtic is not the easiest of matches in which to make a debut.
Dibble plays not only because of Goram's injury but also because the deputy goalkeeper, Dutchman Theo Snelders, injured himself in the warm-up before Rangers Scottish Cup tie with Celtic last week.
Rangers could also be without skipper Richard Gough and defender David Robertson. Long-term injuries mean Paul Gascoigne and Stuart McCall are still some way from full fitness.
Celtic, by comparison, have only one major injury in the lead-up to a game they dare not lose.
Their main injury worries concern striker Paolo di Canio, who strained a hamstring in the 2-0 Cup win over Rangers which kept him out of the defeat at Kilmarnock on Tuesday.

Celtic have closed the gap at the top to five points and were given a helping hand this week when Rangers lost at home to Dundee United just 24 hours after Celtic went down by the same score at Kilmarnock.

That defeat means Rangers go into the game without a win for three matches and their slump in form could yet cost them the chance to emulate Celtic's record-setting haul of nine successive titles achieved between 1965 and 1974.
